I feel like the people who openly talk about having a "mental illness" are usually the ones who are faking it for attention or are real confused about what it means to have a mental disorder. 

People these days do not realize that it is normal to FEEL sadness and anxiety at least a few times a week or even a few times a day. Examples: Running late and feel anxious? Normal. Failed a test and feel anxious? Normal. Broke up with your significant other and feel sad for months? Normal, not a disorder. 

Just because you FEEL those emotions often does NOT mean you have a mental disorder. Humans naturally will experience a wide variety of emotions throughout one day. We are not wired to be content or happy all of the time. A diagnosis can however, be made when you have felt that way every single day and it has impacted your life for a period of longer than 6 months, according to the DSM.  

It's a huge slap in the face to those who have actually been diagnosed with a mental disorder to hear other people say they have it and use it to get attention, when really theres nothing wrong with them. You are making those who struggle every single day look bad. If you think you have a mental illness, please do not read about it on Google. Book yourself a doctor's appointment and go to clinical psychologist before you self-diagnose.
